articles.description:
What is “AI Slop”?


AI Slop is code that looks legitimate but carries little causal weight.
It’s not “broken.”

It’s not “malicious.”

It’s just convincingly empty.
It often shows up as:
promises outrunning evidence (“production-ready”, “scalable”)
tests that exist, but don’t hit real dependencies
structure and documentation growing faster than implementation
This release exists because of a thoughtful comment from OnlineProxy (https://onlineproxy.io/).
They described a “complete-looking” repo with green CI that still felt hollow—and pointed out the real red flag:
CI is green, but 0 integration tests hit real dependencies.
That’s not a nitpick. It’s a real production failure mode.
So I treated that feedback like a bug report—and shipped v2.6.2 as the patch.
“Tests exist” isn’t enough.

v2…
articles.title: AI Slop Detector v2.6.2: Integration Test Evidence (because “green CI” can still be hollow)

articles.author: Mohd Asif Ansari
articles.description:
You know git add and git commit. But what actually happens when you run these commands?
Let's look inside Git and understand how it really works.
When you run git init, Git creates a hidden .git folder. This folder is where Git stores everything about your project.
See it:
ls -la    # On Linux/Mac
dir /a    # On Windows

.git/
├── HEAD              # Points to current branch
├── config            # Repository settings
├── objects/          # All your data (commits, files)
├── refs/             # Branch pointers
├── index             # Staging area
└── logs/             # Change history

Most important:
objects/: Where Git stores all data
refs/: Where branch pointers live
HEAD: Shows your current position
index: Your staging area
Rule: Never manually edit files in .git. Let Git handle it.
G…
articles.title: Inside Git: How It Works and the Role of the .git Folder

articles.author: Whistle_Missile2
articles.description:
Hey everyone,
If you manage your music playlists on YouTube, you’ve probably experienced this frustration: You open an old playlist and find tracks faded out with labels like "[Deleted Video]" or "[Private Video]".
You can't remember what song it was, it won't play, and taking screenshots of every single song for backup is just too much work.
So, I built a free managed service called "FixMyPlaylist" to solve this.
It tracks all unavailable videos (deletions, privacy changes, region locks, etc.), identifies the missing tracks, and automatically replaces them with the best matching alternatives found via my custom ranking algorithm.
How to use it:
Go to FixMyPlaylist.com and log in with your Google account.


Grant the necessary permissions (required for the app to work).
Select the playlists you want to protect, and you're done.
From then on, it automatically scans your playlists once a day, detects any broken videos, and swaps them with valid alternatives.
⚠️ Important Note: The service tracks and recovers videos that become unavailable after registration. Any videos already unavailable at registration will be cleaned up during the next sync cycle with a cleanup record provided.
Q: Why not just use YouTube Music?
While YouTube and YouTube Music are compatible, YTM has some limitations:
Limited Customization: YTM often overrides your preferred versions (live performances, covers, specific mixes) with its "Official Audio" picks.
Silent Deletion: YTM removes deleted/private tracks from the list entirely without notifying you, so you don't even realize a song is gone.
Q: Is it safe?
Yes. This service has passed Google's OAuth Sensitive Scope Verification, YouTube API ToS Review and Quota Increase Approval(Check the video for details).
For more details regarding daily quotas and specific operational questions, please refer to the FAQ in the site.
articles.title: YouTube keeps deleting my music, so I built a service to restore them automatically
